title: Privacy-Fencing for Observability Streams: Dynamic Field Redaction, Access Tracing, and Retention Enforcement
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a privacy-fencing layer across observability streams (traces, metrics, logs) that enforces dynamic field-level redaction rules, tenant-aware retention policies, and immutable access-tracing (who/what/when) for audit. This ticket covers schema for redaction rules, a runtime filter hook for tracing and logging libraries, RBAC checks for downstream pipeline consumers, and retention enforcement in the pipeline storage layer.

Scope:
- Define canonical redaction rule format (allowlist/denylist, regex, transform, pseudonymize) that can be scoped per-tenant, per-environment, and per-stream type.
- Implement tracing/logging SDK hook to apply redaction at source for high-sensitivity fields (PII tokens, emails, credit-card-like sequences).
- Add an access-tracing header + immutable audit record for any process that reads raw observability events.
- Enforce retention via policy engine in the pipeline (tiered retention with eviction hooks for long-term stores).
- Integrate RBAC checks in pipeline consumer registration so only authorized services may access de-identified vs raw views.

Non-goals: full GUI for policy editing (separate PM ticket), building a new long-term cold storage backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- Redaction rule format documented in Confluence and validated by two sample rule sets.
- SDK hook added to tracing and logging libs; sample microservice demonstrates redaction of email and SSN-like patterns before send.
- Pipeline rejects consumer registrations without RBAC token; audit record created for each read and queryable from Console.
- Retention rules applied to test dataset (24h/7d/90d tiers) with automated eviction observed in staging dashboards.
- Integration tests and e2e scenario demonstrating tenant-scoped retention and redaction.

Rollout plan:
1) Beta in staging with one internal tenant, monitor CPU/latency impact (+goal: <5% p50 overhead).
2) Canary to a small set of customers on Dedicated.
3) Full rollout after 2-week stability window and security signoff.

Metrics to track:
- Redaction false-positive/false-negative rates from labeled evaluation sets.
- Latency P50/P95 overhead introduced by SDK hook and pipeline policy checks.
- Number of access-trace records generated per read (cost and storage).
- Policy evaluation errors/failures per 10k events.

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-redaction breaking debugging visibility: provide an escape hatch to request signed access (audit + TTL).
- Performance regressions: implement sampling and move heavy transforms to async worker.
- Policy misconfiguration: ship with safe default denylist and staging validation step.
